packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, isolated image-only reader (Claude Code subagent)
text:
PACKET 16 - unverified image reading

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of the text or an earlier reading. One thing visible inside the images themselves should be declared: image-011/012 show a printed paper label on the host volume reading "Ea" over "1[.]" (second digit cut off, "6" or "7"?), i.e. part of a shelfmark of the host book. I did not use it for anything. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..012 of this packet (I listed the image filenames in the packet directory; packet.json was not read). Beyond simple viewing, I cut the native-resolution images into quadrant and region crops in a scratch directory to look closer. No web, search, catalogue or edition was used. I have deliberately not tried to name the work, including for the red running title transcribed below.

IMAGE MAP
The images come in pairs: an odd-numbered reduced overview and the following even-numbered native-resolution version of the same shot (not a different area).
- image-001/002: view down into the spine cavity (hollow) of a bound book: a parchment piece with 5-6 lines of writing, above the sewn endband.
- image-003/004: closer view of the right half of the same piece (overlaps image-001/002; same lines, not new text).
- image-005/006: view into the cavity from another direction: a larger written parchment surface, about 12-13 lines visible, with a red line at the top; strongly curved, in focus only in a central band.
- image-007/008: head of a written page inside the cavity, with a red running title and about 12 lines beneath, plus part of an adjoining column or page at left and right edges.
- image-009/010: the same page head as 007/008 from a lower left angle (same lines, not new text), showing more of the neighbouring written surface at lower left.
- image-011/012: exterior photograph of the damaged spine/board corner of the host volume, showing manuscript waste both as a spine lining (under the sewing threads, with a red rubric) and on the inside of the lifted cover, plus a fragment with a red initial at right.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation unless marked)
- These are in situ photographs of manuscript waste used as binding material (spine lining and/or cover lining) inside a later binding. No ruler is present; sizes cannot be given. All shots are oblique, curved and partly out of focus.
- Orientation: in image-001..004 the writing is upside down relative to the photograph (letter forms such as "g", "p", "d" are inverted). In image-007..010 the page is upright, slightly rotated. In image-005/006 the lines run across the frame roughly upright but foreshortened. In image-011/012 the spine-lining text runs across the spine and appears upside down or sideways depending on the piece.
- Columns: image-007..010 show one text block with a ruled vertical boundary at its right and a neighbouring block beyond it at both left (image-009 lower left) and right (image-007 right edge), so the leaf is probably in two or more columns (tentative).
- Running title: image-007..010 have a red running title above the block, in two parts set left and right.
- Rubrics: red line or rubric at the top of the surface in image-005/006 (out of focus); a red rubric line in the spine lining in image-011/012; a red penwork initial or paraph on the loose-looking fragment at the right of image-011/012.
- Script: a small, formal gothic book hand in black ink (image-005..010), Latin as far as the abbreviations show. The piece in image-001..004 is in a paler brown-grey ink and may be a different piece or hand (cannot decide from these photographs).
- No glosses, underlining or enlarged initials are visible, apart from a slightly larger capital beginning the first line under the running title.

SELECTION
Selected: the page head in image-007..010 (running title and first lines), since it is the only area with a heading and reasonably sharp focus. Attempted but largely unread: image-001..004, image-005/006, image-011/012.

TRANSCRIPTION

A. Page head (image-008 native; the same lines recur in image-010 and in the overviews image-007/009 - these are repeats, not additional text). Line numbers counted from the top of image-008.

image-008 running title, left part (red): [looped letter with a cross-stroke, ? "L" with abbreviation = "li(ber)"?, or a paraph] . xiiij(?) .   (the numeral is a row of minims ending in a long j: "xiiij"/"xiij"/"riiij"; first stroke is x-shaped)
image-008 running title, right part (red): mach'(?) .   (letters "m a c/t h/b" then a final abbreviation sign like "3"/"z" with a point: "mach3."/"mac3."/"matz."; I do not expand it)

image-008 line 1: R(?)/A(?) t(ri)ce[...]i(?) d(?)m̃(?)/duū(?) q(ui)nte(?)/ginita(?) . cen(?)[...]   (large capital first; then a word with superscript abbreviation; "qnite"/"gnite" with a mark above; a point; "cen"/"can" running to the column edge)
image-008 line 2: S(?)[...]ba(?)/sala(?)[...] . ducē(?)/anne(?) m(i)l(i)a(?)/milĩ . bis(?)/lia   (two points divide the line into three groups; the middle group has abbreviation strokes above)
image-008 line 3: [...]ica(?) t(ri)ci(n)ta(?)/teicia do(?) i(?)[...]ne(?) . ma(?)[...]
image-008 line 4: [...]A(?)b(?) [...] sept(?)/sexc(?) m(i)lia(?)/ml'ie q(ui)(?)/eq(?) n(?)a(?)[...]
image-008 line 5: m(?)[...] A(?)hera(?)/thera(?) m(?) . B(?)n(?)/Ben(?) . [...]   (points between short groups)
image-008 line 6: Ca(?) B(?) [...]india(?)/indman(?) . Rapsa(?)/Kapsa(?)[...]   (a word beginning with a clear capital R or K after a point)
image-008 line 7: [...] B(?)/b(?) [...]aduna(?)/adiutore(?) . [...]
image-008 line 8: [...] b(?)r(?) [...]uadem(?)/nadon(?) illa(?)/ille [...]
image-008 line 9: [...] h(?)[...] Karissim(?)/barisan(?) [...] ii(?) [...]
image-008 lines 10-12: [illegible - out of focus and under a green-grey stain]
Character of the passage (observation, tentative): short word groups separated by points, several numerals or number words with "m(i)lia"-like abbreviations, and capitals after points; it looks like an enumeration or list rather than continuous argument. I cannot confirm any single number.

Neighbouring surface at lower left of image-010 (separate block; line ends only):
image-010, left block, successive lines: [...]tin(?) / [...]bet(?)/het(?) / [...]oem(?) / [...]n(?) / [...]dels(?)/ucls(?) / [...]ence(?) / [...]
(a faint red letter or stroke at the top of this block)

B. Larger surface (image-006 native; image-005 overview is the same shot). Only a central band is in focus. Line numbers counted from the top of image-006.
image-006 line 1 (red, out of focus): [red rubric or running title, two groups, illegible]
image-006 lines 2-4: [illegible - out of focus]
image-006 line 5: [...] ...then(?)/thou(?)[...] sua(?)/sita(?) ... R(?)de(?)[...]
image-006 line 6: [...] Ca(?) q(?)uoni(?)a(?)/minima(?) ... ru(?)...
image-006 line 7: [...] G(?)/E(?) Dinma(?)/Duma(?)[...] ... ince(?)[...]
image-006 line 8: [...] ...tan(?) t(?)ies(?) om(?)... m(?)...
image-006 line 9: [...] ...bens(?)/lcias(?) sala(?)/salm(?) ... in(?) ...
image-006 line 10: [...] ...u . Ne(?)/Re(?)ca(n)t(ur)(?)/Vocaū(?) u(?) ...   (a point, then a capital, then a word with a horizontal abbreviation stroke)
image-006 lines 11-13: [...] ...mb(?)... / ...nti(?)... / ...p(?)ac(?)a(?) eni(?)/cui ...   [increasingly out of focus]
None of these is secure; the photograph does not resolve the letters.

C. Piece above the endband (image-002 and image-004 native; overlapping views of the same lines). The writing is upside down in the photographs; I read it by mental rotation only, and the results are very uncertain. Lines listed in the order they appear from the top of image-002 as displayed (which is the reverse of the true reading order).
image-002 displayed line 1: [...] ...pa(?)... [...]pn(?) ...
image-002 displayed line 2: [...] ...niinp(?)... eo(?) g(?) ...
image-002 displayed line 3: [...] ...nuiy(?)... ...ae(?) ...
image-002 displayed line 4: [...] ...v(?)tu(?)...
image-002 displayed line 5: [illegible]
On the adjoining strip at the right of image-004 (line ends of a second piece or column): four or five fragments, illegible.
These are shapes as seen inverted, given only so that a later reader can confirm which piece is meant; they are not readings.

D. Exterior view (image-012 native; image-011 overview)
- Printed label on the host volume: "Ea" / "1[6?]" (modern printed shelf label, partly hidden).
- Spine lining under the sewing threads: about ten lines of small gothic script, with one red rubric line of two or three words about a third of the way down; out of focus and crossed by the threads. I can make out no word with confidence. The red rubric shows an "x"-like letter and a word with tall strokes.
- Inside of the lifted cover (upper centre): five or six lines of the same kind of script, sharply foreshortened; illegible.
- Fragment at right: a red penwork initial or paraph (round, "D"/"O"-like) beside a dark brown stain, with three or four faint line-ends below; illegible.

UNREAD AREAS
Everything except the first nine lines of the page head in image-008/010 remains effectively unread; even those nine lines are tentative.

LIMITATIONS
- All images are oblique endoscope-style or macro photographs into a binding cavity with very shallow depth of field; most of each frame is out of focus, and the parchment is curved, stained (green and yellow mould or adhesive) and partly covered by sewing structure.
- No scale. Orientation differs between shots. Column order and how the several written surfaces relate to one another (one leaf or several) cannot be determined.
- The red running title is the best anchor ("[sign] . xiiij(?) ." on the left, "mach'(?)." on the right), followed by a first line beginning with a large capital and containing "... q(ui)nte(?) . cen...". Both are uncertain in detail.
- Useful next images: the page head of image-007/008 retaken square-on and in focus for the full column width; a straight-on focused shot of the surface in image-005/006; and image-001..004 rotated 180 degrees with the lens parallel to the parchment.
